scripts/main.py:
"""
Snake River watershed web map.

The six sampled source catchments above the Weiser confluence, colored by one of several
results, with the rivers and sample sites as overlays. Clicking a watershed opens its stats:
modelled contribution to the sink, polymer mix (against the sink's), land cover and stream
connectivity. The data come from export_web_map.py in the main project; the pieces live in the
`webmap` package and this module only assembles them.
"""
import js
from pyodide.ffi import create_proxy

from antioch import DOM
from antioch.elements import Div
from webmap import Sidebar, WatershedMap
from webmap import config as c

INITIAL = "basin"


def main():
    DOM.clear()
    DOM.title = "Snake River Microplastics"
    DOM.body.style.update(c.BODY_STYLE)

    sidebar = Sidebar(INITIAL)
    world = WatershedMap(INITIAL)
    sidebar.on_select = world.color_by
    app = Div(sidebar.element, Div(world.element, style=c.MAP_PANE_STYLE), style=c.APP_STYLE)
    DOM.add(app)

    # Inline styles have no media queries, so the layout follows the window width here.
    narrow = js.window.matchMedia(c.NARROW)

    def layout(*args):
        app.style.update(c.APP_NARROW if narrow.matches else c.APP_WIDE)
        sidebar.set_narrow(narrow.matches)

    layout()
    narrow.addEventListener("change", create_proxy(layout))


main()

"""
Splash screen: static HTML shown while Pyodide loads (antioch.toml splash_file), as in Sed/Stats.
"""

from antioch.static import StaticPage, Div, P, keyframe, rotate, opacity, translateY

# River blue fading into the light gray of the map's basemap.
DEEP_BLUE = "#1f4e79"
RIVER_BLUE = "#2f6fa8"
MIST = "#9fb8cf"
FONT = '-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif'


@keyframe
def spin():
    rotate({0: 0, 100: 360})


@keyframe
def fadeInUp():
    opacity({0: 0, 100: 1})
    translateY({0: 20, 100: 0})


def generate_splash():
    """Generate the static splash screen HTML."""
    page = StaticPage(title="Snake River Watersheds", lang="en")
    page.set_title("Snake River Watersheds")
    page.add_meta(name="viewport", content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0")
    page.set_description("An interactive map of microplastic sources in the Snake River above "
                         "the Weiser River confluence: polymer mixes, land cover, stream "
                         "connectivity and modelled contributions of six source watersheds.")
    page.set_keywords("microplastics", "Snake River", "watersheds", "mixture modeling",
                      "land cover", "Idaho")
    page.set_author("Ryan Nielsen")
    page.add_style(spin.render())
    page.add_style(fadeInUp.render())

    background = Div(style={
        "margin": "0",
        "padding": "0 16px",
        "font_family": FONT,
        "background": f"linear-gradient(160deg, {DEEP_BLUE} 0%, {RIVER_BLUE} 55%, {MIST} 100%)",
        "min_height": "100vh",
        "display": "flex",
        "justify_content": "center",
        "align_items": "center",
        "color": "white",
    })
    container = Div(id="loading-splash", style={
        "text-align": "center",
        "max-width": "560px",
    })
    title = Div("Microplastics in the Snake River Watershed", style={
        "font-size": "2.4em",
        "font-weight": "bold",
        "line-height": "1.2",
        "margin-bottom": "16px",
        "animation": "fadeInUp 0.8s ease-out both",
    })
    tagline = P("Six source watersheds, one downstream sample, and where its plastics came from",
                style={
                    "font-size": "1.2em",
                    "margin": "0 0 32px",
                    "opacity": "0.9",
                    "animation": "fadeInUp 0.8s ease-out 0.2s both",
                })
    spinner = Div(style={
        "border": "4px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3)",
        "border-top": "4px solid white",
        "border-radius": "50%",
        "width": "48px",
        "height": "48px",
        "animation": "spin 1s linear infinite",
        "margin": "0 auto 16px",
    })
    loading = P("Loading the map...", style={"font-size": "1em", "margin": "0", "opacity": "0.8"})

    container.add(title, tagline, spinner, loading)
    background.add(container)
    page.add(background)
    return page


# Run directly to preview the splash screen.
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    from pathlib import Path

    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
    preview = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "splash_preview.html"
    preview.write_text(generate_splash().render())
    print(f"Splash screen preview saved to: {preview}")

"""The study's results, as exported by export_web_map.py into assets/."""
import json


def read_asset(name):
    """Text of an asset; Antioch copies assets/ into Pyodide's filesystem at /assets."""
    with open(f"/assets/{name}") as f:
        return f.read()


WATERSHEDS_TEXT = read_asset("watersheds.geojson")
RIVERS_TEXT = read_asset("rivers.geojson")
SAMPLES_TEXT = read_asset("samples.geojson")
CONFIG = json.loads(read_asset("layers.json"))

WATERSHEDS = json.loads(WATERSHEDS_TEXT)
PROPS = {f["properties"]["id"]: f["properties"] for f in WATERSHEDS["features"]}
LAYERS = {layer["id"]: layer for layer in CONFIG["layers"]}
POLYMERS = CONFIG["polymers"]
SINK = CONFIG["sink"]
MODEL = CONFIG["model"]


def bounds():
    """[[south, west], [north, east]] of the watersheds."""
    points = []
    for feature in WATERSHEDS["features"]:
        geometry = feature["geometry"]
        polygons = [geometry["coordinates"]] if geometry["type"] == "Polygon" \
            else geometry["coordinates"]
        points += [pt for polygon in polygons for ring in polygon for pt in ring]
    lons, lats = [p[0] for p in points], [p[1] for p in points]
    return [[min(lats), min(lons)], [max(lats), max(lons)]]

"""Point labels on the canvas legends that step aside instead of overlapping."""

# Where to try a label, relative to its point (pixels): right of it, then above and below.
OFFSETS = [(9, 0), (9, -11), (9, 11), (9, -22), (9, 22)]
HEIGHT = 11  # label box height


def place_label(ctx, text, x, y, placed):
    """Draw text beside (x, y) at the first offset whose box misses every box in placed (and
    add its box there); if none is free, at the first offset."""
    width = ctx.measureText(text).width
    boxes = [(x + dx, y + dy - HEIGHT / 2, width, HEIGHT) for dx, dy in OFFSETS]
    box = next((b for b in boxes if not any(_overlap(b, other) for other in placed)), boxes[0])
    placed.append(box)
    ctx.textAlign = "left"
    ctx.textBaseline = "middle"
    ctx.fillText(text, box[0], box[1] + HEIGHT / 2)


def _overlap(a, b):
    return a[0] < b[0] + b[2] and b[0] < a[0] + a[2] and a[1] < b[1] + b[3] and b[1] < a[1] + a[3]

"""The Leaflet map: basemaps, the watersheds (recolored on demand), rivers and sample sites.""" import js from antioch.event import when from antioch.macros import Map from pyodide.ffi import create_proxy, to_js from . import config as c from .data import PROPS, RIVERS_TEXT, SAMPLES_TEXT, SINK, WATERSHEDS_TEXT, bounds from .popup import Popup # Keyless basemaps (CARTO's now needs an API key): Esri light gray first, imagery as an option. ESRI = "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/{}/MapServer/tile/{{z}}/{{y}}/{{x}}" BASEMAPS = { "Light gray": (ESRI.format("Canvas/World_Light_Gray_Base"), "Tiles © Esri — Esri, HERE, Garmin, © OpenStreetMap " "contributors", 16), "Satellite": (ESRI.format("World_Imagery"), "Tiles © Esri", 18), } # State lines and place names, drawn over the watersheds (transparent tiles). REFERENCE = ESRI.format("Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places_Alternate") # Map panes (Leaflet z-index): the reference above the watersheds and rivers (overlay pane, # 400), the sample dots above that so labels never cover them; popups stay on top (700). PANES = {"reference": 420, "samples": 450} MIN_ZOOM_SLACK = 1 # zoom levels the viewer may go out past the fitted view PAN_MARGIN = 1.0 # panning stops this far past the study area (fraction of its size) MAP_STYLE = {"display": "block", "border": "none", "border_radius": "0"} def js_obj(d): return to_js(d, dict_converter=js.Object.fromEntries) class WatershedMap: """ Attributes: element - the map's root element layer - id of the coloring the watersheds are drawn in """ def __init__(self, layer): self.layer = layer self._features = {} # watershed id -> Leaflet layer self._popups = {} # watershed id, or "sink" -> its Popup while open self._contents = {} # the same keys -> the popup's content function (a JS proxy) self._sink = None # the sink sample's marker self._proxies = [] # JS callbacks, kept alive self._map = Map(center=[43.9, -115.6], zoom=7, width="100%", height="100%", container_style=MAP_STYLE) self.element = self._map.element @when(self._map.events.ready) def on_ready(sender, *args): leaflet = self._map._get_state("map_instance") for name, z in PANES.items(): pane = leaflet.createPane(name) pane.style.zIndex = str(z) pane.style.pointerEvents = "none" # clicks reach the watersheds below self._add_watersheds() self._add_rivers() self._add_samples(leaflet) self._add_basemaps(leaflet) self._map.fit_bounds(bounds()) # No zooming out past the whole study area, and no panning away from it. (south, west), (north, east) = bounds() area = js.L.latLngBounds(js_obj([south, west]), js_obj([north, east])) leaflet.setMinZoom(leaflet.getBoundsZoom(area) - MIN_ZOOM_SLACK) leaflet.setMaxBounds(area.pad(PAN_MARGIN)) leaflet.options.maxBoundsViscosity = 1.0 # a hard edge, not a rubber band def color_by(self, layer): """Redraw the watersheds in coloring `layer`, and any open popup with its stats.""" self.layer = layer for wid, feature in self._features.items(): feature.setStyle(self._style(wid)) for key, owner in [*self._features.items(), ("sink", self._sink)]: if owner is not None and owner.isPopupOpen(): self._popups.pop(key).closed() # The content function again, not a built element: Leaflet keeps whatever it # is given, and a fixed element would stop later openings rebuilding the stats. owner.setPopupContent(self._contents[key]) self._popups[key].opened() def _popup(self, key): """The DOM content of a popup (a watershed id, or "sink") under the current coloring.""" self._popups[key] = (Popup(SINK, self.layer, sink=True) if key == "sink" else Popup(PROPS[key], self.layer)) return self._popups[key].element.dom_element def _bind_popup(self, layer, key): """Give a Leaflet layer the popup for key. It is built when opened, so it shows the stats of the coloring at that moment; its charts are drawn once it is in the page, and freed when it closes.""" self._contents[key] = self._proxy(lambda _: self._popup(key)) layer.bindPopup(self._contents[key], js_obj({"maxWidth": 340, "autoPanPaddingTopLeft": [60, 20]})) layer.on("popupopen", self._proxy(lambda e: self._popups[key].opened())) layer.on("popupclose", self._proxy(lambda e: self._popups.pop(key).closed() if key in self._popups else None)) def _proxy(self, fn): proxy = create_proxy(fn) self._proxies.append(proxy) return proxy def _style(self, wid, weight=1.5): return js_obj({"color": c.OUTLINE, "weight": weight, "opacity": 1, "fillColor": PROPS[wid]["fill"][self.layer], "fillOpacity": c.FILL_OPACITY}) def _add_watersheds(self): def each(feature, layer): wid = feature.properties.id self._features[wid] = layer layer.setStyle(self._style(wid)) self._bind_popup(layer, wid) layer.on("mouseover", self._proxy(lambda e: layer.setStyle(self._style(wid, 3)))) layer.on("mouseout", self._proxy(lambda e: layer.setStyle(self._style(wid)))) self._map.add_geojson(js.JSON.parse(WATERSHEDS_TEXT), name="Watersheds", on_each_feature=each, add_to_control=False) def _add_rivers(self): def each(feature, layer): order = feature.properties.sorder layer.setStyle(js_obj({"color": c.RIVER, "weight": 0.6 + 0.55 * (order - 4), "opacity": 0.85})) self._map.add_geojson(js.JSON.parse(RIVERS_TEXT), name="Rivers", on_each_feature=each) def _add_samples(self, leaflet): def marker(feature, latlng): p = feature.properties size = {"radius": 8, "weight": 2} if p.sink else {"radius": 6, "weight": 1.5} return js.L.circleMarker(latlng, js_obj({**size, "fillColor": p.color, "color": c.OUTLINE, "fillOpacity": 1, "pane": "samples"})) def each(feature, layer): p = feature.properties if p.sink: self._sink = layer self._bind_popup(layer, "sink") else: layer.bindPopup(f"{p.sample_id}
{p.site}
a source in the mixture " "model") # Map.add_geojson takes no pointToLayer, so the circles are built directly. samples = js.L.geoJSON(js.JSON.parse(SAMPLES_TEXT), js_obj({ "pointToLayer": self._proxy(marker), "onEachFeature": self._proxy(each)})) samples.addTo(leaflet) self._map._add_to_layer_control(samples, "Sample sites") def _add_basemaps(self, leaflet): """Swap the macro's default tiles for BASEMAPS, all offered in the layer control, and add the REFERENCE overlay (on by default).""" leaflet.eachLayer(self._proxy(lambda layer: leaflet.removeLayer(layer) if hasattr(layer, "getTileUrl") else None)) control = self._map._get_state("layer_control") for i, (name, (url, attribution, max_zoom)) in enumerate(BASEMAPS.items()): tiles = js.L.tileLayer(url, js_obj({"attribution": attribution, "maxZoom": max_zoom})) if i == 0: tiles.addTo(leaflet) control.addBaseLayer(tiles, name) reference = js.L.tileLayer(REFERENCE, js_obj({"pane": "reference", "maxZoom": 16})) reference.addTo(leaflet) control.addOverlay(reference, "State lines & places")
scripts/webmap/plotly_chart.py:
"""Plotly-backed chart macro, as in sed_stats' plot_lib.

Uses the `basic` bundle (bar, pie, scatter): the popups only draw bars. Built lazily
(lazy_init): a popup's content is only attached to the page when it opens, and Plotly needs its
div in the document to lay out, so the map calls ensure_initialized() then.
"""
import js
from antioch.elements import Div
from antioch.macros.js_library import JSLibraryMacro


class PlotlyChart(JSLibraryMacro):
    """
    Usage:
        chart = PlotlyChart(traces=[{"type": "bar", "x": ["a"], "y": [1]}], width=300,
                            height=220)
        parent.add(chart.element)
        chart.ensure_initialized()  # once chart.element is in the document
    """

    def __init__(self, traces=None, layout=None, config=None, width=300, height=220, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(macro_type="plotly_chart", lazy_init=True, **kwargs)
        self._set_state(traces=traces or [], layout=layout or {}, config=config or {},
                        width=width, height=height)
        self._init_macro()

    def _get_library_dependencies(self):
        return {"scripts": ["antioch/lib/vendor/plotly-basic.min.js"], "stylesheets": []}

    def _get_library_global_name(self):
        return "Plotly"

    def _create_elements(self):
        # Sized up front so the popup doesn't change size when the plot draws.
        size = {"width": f"{self._get_state('width')}px",
                "height": f"{self._get_state('height')}px"}
        container = self._register_element("container", self._create_container(
            {**size, "display": "block"}))
        holder = self._register_element("holder", Div(style=size))
        holder.set_attribute("id", f"plotly_{self._id}")
        container.add(holder)
        return container

    def _build_layout(self):
        layout = {
            "width": self._get_state("width"),
            "height": self._get_state("height"),
            "margin": {"l": 40, "r": 8, "t": 8, "b": 60},
            "font": {"size": 11},
            "hovermode": "closest",
            "paper_bgcolor": "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
            "plot_bgcolor": "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        }
        layout.update(self._get_state("layout"))
        return layout

    def _build_config(self):
        config = {"displaylogo": False, "displayModeBar": False, "responsive": False}
        config.update(self._get_state("config"))
        return config

    def _create_js_instance(self):
        # Plotly's API is keyed on the graph div itself, so that element is the instance.
        graph_div = self._get_element("holder")._dom_element
        js.Plotly.newPlot(graph_div, self._to_js(self._get_state("traces")),
                          self._to_js(self._build_layout()), self._to_js(self._build_config()))
        return graph_div

    def _cleanup_js_instance(self):
        if self.js_instance:
            js.Plotly.purge(self.js_instance)
scripts/webmap/popup.py:
"""The stats a watershed (or the sink sample) shows when clicked, built as Antioch elements for a
Leaflet popup: a header, then only the stats behind the map's current coloring."""
from antioch.elements import Div, H3, Span

from . import config as c
from .data import MODEL, POLYMERS, PROPS, SINK
from .plotly_chart import PlotlyChart


def _bar(label, value, scale, color, text):
    """One labelled bar."""
    track = Div(Div(style={**c.BAR_FILL_STYLE, "width": f"{_percent(value, scale)}%",
                           "background-color": color}),
                style=c.BAR_TRACK_STYLE)
    return Div(Span(label), track, Span(text, style=c.VALUE_STYLE), style=c.BAR_ROW_STYLE)


def _percent(value, scale):
    return 0 if scale <= 0 else min(100.0, 100 * value / scale)


def _heading(text):
    return Div(text, style=c.POPUP_HEADING_STYLE)


def _shares(values, fmt):
    return [_bar(c.SHARE_LABELS[k], values[k], 1, c.SHARE_COLORS[k], fmt(values[k]))
            for k in c.SHARE_LABELS]


def _stats(rows):
    grid = Div(style=c.STAT_GRID_STYLE)
    for label, value in rows:
        grid.add(Span(label), Span(value, style=c.VALUE_STYLE))
    return grid


def _bar_chart(trace, charts):
    """A Plotly bar chart of one trace, its y axis in percent, with hover values but fixed axes
    (no zooming); added to charts so the popup can draw and free it."""
    chart = PlotlyChart(
        traces=[{"type": "bar", **trace}],
        layout={"bargap": 0.25, "showlegend": False, "dragmode": False,
                "font": {"family": c.FONT, "size": 11, "color": c.POPUP_INK},
                "yaxis": {"tickformat": ".0%", "gridcolor": c.TRACK, "zeroline": False,
                          "fixedrange": True},
                "xaxis": {"tickangle": -45, "fixedrange": True},
                "margin": {"l": 40, "r": 8, "t": 8, "b": 58}},
        config={"scrollZoom": False, "doubleClick": False},
        width=300, height=210)
    charts.append(chart)
    return chart.element


def _polymers(p, charts):
    """This sample's polymer mix."""
    return [_heading("Polymer mix (share of particles)"), _bar_chart(
        {"x": POLYMERS, "y": [p["polymers"][q] for q in POLYMERS],
         "marker": {"color": p["color"]}, "hovertemplate": "%{x}: %{y:.1%}<extra></extra>"},
        charts)]


def _model_mix(charts):
    """The sink's modelled mix: each source's contribution, whiskers its bootstrap range."""
    sources = sorted((p for p in PROPS.values() if "contribution" in p),
                     key=lambda p: -p["contribution"])
    best = [p["contribution"] / 100 for p in sources]
    lo, hi = ([p["contribution_range"][i] / 100 for p in sources] for i in (0, 1))
    return [_heading("Modelled sources of this sample"), _bar_chart(
        {"x": [p["name"].split(" (")[0].replace(" River", "") for p in sources], "y": best,
         "marker": {"color": [p["dot_color"] for p in sources]},  # as the sample dots
         "error_y": {"type": "data", "symmetric": False, "thickness": 1.2, "width": 4,
                     "color": c.POPUP_MUTED, "array": [h - b for h, b in zip(hi, best)],
                     "arrayminus": [b - l for b, l in zip(best, lo)]},
         "customdata": [[l, h] for l, h in zip(lo, hi)],
         "hovertemplate": "%{x}: %{y:.0%} (bootstrap %{customdata[0]:.0%}–"
                          "%{customdata[1]:.0%})<extra></extra>"}, charts),
        Div("Optimised best fit of the polymer mixture model; whiskers: bootstrap 16–84%.",
            style=c.META_STYLE)]


def _source_likeness():
    """How alike each source alone is to the sink, beside the modelled mix's fit (above)."""
    sources = sorted((p for p in PROPS.values() if "likeness" in p), key=lambda p: -p["likeness"])
    return [_heading("Each source alone vs. this sample"),
            _stats([(p["name"], f"{p['likeness']:.3f}") for p in sources])]


def _not_for_sink(what):
    return lambda p, charts: [_heading(what), Div(
        "Computed for each source catchment, not for the sink, which receives all six.",
        style=c.META_STYLE)]


def _contribution(p):
    lo, hi = p["contribution_range"]
    return [_heading("Contribution to the sink"),
            Div(Span(f"{p['contribution']:.0f}%", style=c.BIG_STYLE),
                Span(f"bootstrap range {lo:.0f}–{hi:.0f}%", style=c.RANGE_STYLE))]


def _connectivity(p):
    return [_heading("Stream connectivity"),
            _stats([("Connected on sampling day", f"{p['connected_sampling']:.0%}"),
                    ("Connected, year average", f"{p['connected_annual']:.0%}"),
                    ("Stream length mapped", f"{p['stream_km']:,.0f} km")])]


# coloring (layers.json id) -> the stats behind it; each takes the properties and a list to
# add any Plotly charts it builds to
SECTIONS = {
    "basin": _polymers,
    "whole": lambda p, charts: [_heading("Land cover, whole watershed"),
                                *_shares(p["whole"], lambda v: f"{v:.1%}")],
    "corridor": lambda p, charts: [_heading("Land-cover score along connected streams"),
                                   *_shares(p["corridor"], lambda v: f"{v:.3f}")],
    "contribution": lambda p, charts: _contribution(p),
    "likeness": lambda p, charts: [_heading("Likeness to the sink"), _stats([
        ("This sample alone vs. the sink", f"{p['likeness']:.3f}")])],
    "connected_sampling": lambda p, charts: _connectivity(p),
    "peak": lambda p, charts: [_heading("Flow"),
                               _stats([("Median peak flow", p["peak_flow"])])],
}


# The same for the sink sample, whose catchment is the whole basin above it.
SINK_SECTIONS = {
    "basin": _polymers,
    "whole": lambda p, charts: [_heading("Land cover, whole basin above the sink"),
                                *_shares(p["whole"], lambda v: f"{v:.1%}")],
    "corridor": _not_for_sink("Land-cover score along connected streams"),
    "contribution": lambda p, charts: _model_mix(charts),
    "likeness": lambda p, charts: _source_likeness(),
    "connected_sampling": _not_for_sink("Stream connectivity"),
    "peak": _not_for_sink("Flow"),
}


class Popup:
    """
    A watershed's popup under one coloring; Popup(SINK, layer, sink=True) is the sink sample's.

    Attributes:
        element - the content (an Antioch Div) to hand to Leaflet
    """

    def __init__(self, p, layer, sink=False):
        self._charts = []
        self.element = Div(style=c.POPUP_STYLE)
        title = H3(Span(style={**c.DOT_STYLE, "background-color": p["color"]}), Span(p["name"]),
                   style=c.POPUP_TITLE_STYLE)
        if "sample_id" not in p:
            self.element.add(title, Div("Land draining straight to the Snake between the "
                                        "sample sites; not sampled.", style=c.META_STYLE))
            return
        area = f"{p['area_km2']:,.0f} km²" + (" upstream" if sink else "")
        self.element.add(
            title,
            Div(f"Sample {p['sample_id'][-2:]} · {p['particles']:.0f} particles · {area}",
                style=c.META_STYLE),
        )
        if sink:  # how well the modelled mix of sources reproduces this sample
            self.element.add(_stats([(f"Mixture-model fit ({MODEL['metric']})",
                                      f"{MODEL['best_score']:.3f}")]))
        self.element.add(*(SINK_SECTIONS if sink else SECTIONS)[layer](p, self._charts))

    def opened(self):
        """Draw the charts, now that the content is in the page."""
        for chart in self._charts:
            chart.ensure_initialized()

    def closed(self):
        for chart in self._charts:
            chart.destroy()
        self._charts = []

"""The sidebar: title, the coloring choices, and the chosen coloring's description and legend."""
from antioch.elements import Div, H1, H2, Input, Label, P, Span
from antioch.event import when

from . import config as c
from .data import CONFIG, LAYERS, MODEL
from .ternary_key import ternary_key
from .wheel_key import wheel_key


class Sidebar:
    """
    Attributes:
        element   - the sidebar's root Div
        on_select - called with a layer id when the viewer picks a coloring
    """

    def __init__(self, initial):
        self.on_select = None
        self._current = initial
        self._choices = {}
        self._description = P("", style=c.DESCRIPTION_STYLE)
        self._legend = Div()
        for layer in CONFIG["layers"]:
            self._choices[layer["id"]] = self._choice(layer)
        self.element = Div(
            H1("Microplastics in the Snake River Watershed", style=c.TITLE_STYLE),
            P("I sampled 6 watersheds and the area downstream of them "
              "to determine which watersheds contributed the most microplastics "
              "to the main stem of the Snake.", style=c.LEDE_STYLE),
            H2("Watershed Attributes:", style=c.HEADING_STYLE),
            *self._choices.values(),
            self._description,
            self._legend,
            H2("Information and References:", style=c.HEADING_STYLE),
            P(f"Mixture model: polymer-type unmixing, {MODEL['metric']} "
              f"{MODEL['best_score']:.3f}, optimised best fit with bootstrap ranges. Land cover: "
              "ESA WorldCover 2021. Streams: NHDPlus V2 and high-resolution NHD canals; flow "
              "permanence: USGS PROSPER. Watersheds: MERIT-Hydro.", style=c.FOOTNOTE_STYLE),
            style=c.SIDEBAR_STYLE,
        )
        self.show(initial)

    def _choice(self, layer):
        radio = Input("radio", name="coloring", value=layer["id"], style=c.RADIO_STYLE)
        if layer["id"] == self._current:
            radio.set_attribute("checked", "checked")
        label = Label(radio, Span(layer["title"]), style=c.CHOICE_STYLE)

        @when(radio.events.change)
        def on_change(sender, *args):
            self.show(layer["id"])
            if self.on_select:
                self.on_select(layer["id"])

        @when(label.events.mouseenter)
        def on_enter(sender, *args):
            if layer["id"] != self._current:
                label.style.update({"background-color": c.HOVER})

        @when(label.events.mouseleave)
        def on_leave(sender, *args):
            if layer["id"] != self._current:
                label.style.update(c.CHOICE_IDLE)

        return label

    def show(self, layer_id):
        """Mark layer_id as chosen and show its description and legend."""
        self._current = layer_id
        for lid, label in self._choices.items():
            label.style.update(c.CHOICE_ACTIVE if lid == layer_id else c.CHOICE_IDLE)
        layer = LAYERS[layer_id]
        self._description.set_text(layer["description"])
        self._legend.clear()
        if "gradient" in layer:
            self._legend.add(*_gradient(layer["gradient"]))
        if "ternary" in layer:
            self._legend.add(ternary_key(layer["ternary"]))
        if "wheel" in layer:
            self._legend.add(wheel_key(layer["wheel"]))
        self._legend.add(*[
            Div(Span(style={**c.SWATCH_STYLE, **(c.DOT_SWATCH if item.get("marker") == "dot"
                                                 else {}),
                            "background-color": item["color"]}),
                Span(item["label"]), style=c.LEGEND_ROW_STYLE)
            for item in layer["legend"]])

    def set_narrow(self, narrow):
        self.element.style.update(c.SIDEBAR_NARROW if narrow else c.SIDEBAR_WIDE)


def _gradient(spec):
    """A horizontal color bar with labelled ticks underneath (at: 0-1 along the bar)."""
    bar = Div(style={**c.GRADIENT_STYLE,
                     "background": f"linear-gradient(to right, {', '.join(spec['stops'])})"})
    ticks = Div(style=c.TICKS_STYLE)
    for tick in spec["ticks"]:
        left = f"{100 * tick['at']:.1f}%"
        ticks.add(Div(style={**c.TICK_STYLE, "left": left}),
                  Span(tick["label"], style={**c.TICK_LABEL_STYLE, "left": left}))
    return [bar, ticks]

"""The land-cover legend: the truncated agricultural / urban / wilderness triangle of the land-cover
figures, drawn on a canvas, with each watershed as a dot in its catchment color."""
import math

import js
from antioch.elements import Canvas

from . import config as c
from .labels import place_label
from .data import CONFIG

WIDTH, HEIGHT = 300, 268   # CSS pixels
SIDE = 196                 # triangle side
LEFT = (WIDTH - SIDE) / 2
BASE = HEIGHT - 50         # y of the triangle's base
SQRT3_2 = math.sqrt(3) / 2
GRID_STEP = 0.05           # gridlines and ticks every 5 points of agricultural / urban share
TICK_FONT = f"10.5px {c.FONT}"
CORNER_FONT = f"11px {c.FONT}"
POINT_FONT = f"600 10px {c.FONT}"


def ternary_key(spec):
    """A Canvas drawing the triangle and spec["points"] (x, y in triangle units; color)."""
    ratio = js.window.devicePixelRatio or 1
    canvas = Canvas(width=int(WIDTH * ratio), height=int(HEIGHT * ratio),
                    style={"width": f"{WIDTH}px", "height": f"{HEIGHT}px", "display": "block",
                           "margin": "4px 0 6px"})
    ctx = canvas.dom_element.getContext("2d")
    ctx.scale(ratio, ratio)
    w_min = CONFIG["ternary"]["w_min"]
    span = 1 - w_min

    for cell in CONFIG["ternary"]["cells"]:
        *xy, color = cell
        _path(ctx, list(zip(xy[0::2], xy[1::2])))
        ctx.fillStyle = color
        ctx.strokeStyle = color  # hairline in the same color closes the seams between cells
        ctx.lineWidth = 0.6
        ctx.fill()
        ctx.stroke()

    # Gridlines at each step of agricultural, urban and wilderness share (as on the figures).
    ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7)"
    ctx.lineWidth = 0.8
    steps = [k * GRID_STEP / span for k in range(1, round(span / GRID_STEP))]
    for t in steps:
        for line in ([(1 - t, 0), ((1 - t) / 2, (1 - t) * SQRT3_2)],
                     [(t, 0), (1 - (1 - t) / 2, (1 - t) * SQRT3_2)],
                     [(t / 2, t * SQRT3_2), (1 - t / 2, t * SQRT3_2)]):
            _path(ctx, line, close=False)
            ctx.stroke()

    _path(ctx, [(0, 0), (1, 0), (0.5, SQRT3_2)])
    ctx.strokeStyle = c.INK
    ctx.lineWidth = 1
    ctx.stroke()

    score = spec["score"]
    fmt = (lambda v: f"{v:.2f}") if score else (lambda v: f"{v:.0%}")
    ctx.fillStyle = c.INK_MUTED
    ctx.font = TICK_FONT
    for k, t in enumerate(steps, start=1):
        v = k * GRID_STEP
        _text(ctx, fmt(v), (1 - t, 0), "center", "top", dy=4)                         # ag
        _text(ctx, fmt(v), (1 - (1 - t) / 2, (1 - t) * SQRT3_2), "left", "middle", dx=5)  # urban
        _text(ctx, fmt(w_min + v), (t / 2, t * SQRT3_2), "right", "middle", dx=-5)    # wild.
    ctx.font = CORNER_FONT
    ctx.fillStyle = c.INK
    _text(ctx, f"{fmt(1)} wilderness", (0.5, SQRT3_2), "center", "bottom", dy=-5)
    _text(ctx, f"{fmt(span)} agricultural", (0, 0), "left", "top", dy=20, dx=-30)
    _text(ctx, f"{fmt(span)} urban", (1, 0), "right", "top", dy=20, dx=30)

    placed = []
    for point in spec["points"]:
        x, y = _px(point["x"], point["y"])
        ctx.beginPath()
        ctx.arc(x, y, 5, 0, 2 * math.pi)
        ctx.fillStyle = point["color"]
        ctx.fill()
        ctx.lineWidth = 1.5
        ctx.strokeStyle = c.OUTLINE
        ctx.stroke()
        ctx.beginPath()
        ctx.arc(x, y, 6, 0, 2 * math.pi)
        ctx.lineWidth = 0.75
        ctx.strokeStyle = c.INK
        ctx.stroke()
        # Numbered, to match the legend rows.
        ctx.font = POINT_FONT
        ctx.fillStyle = c.INK
        place_label(ctx, point["label"], x, y, placed)
    return canvas


def _px(x, y):
    return LEFT + x * SIDE, BASE - y * SIDE


def _path(ctx, points, close=True):
    ctx.beginPath()
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(points):
        px, py = _px(x, y)
        if i == 0:
            ctx.moveTo(px, py)
        else:
            ctx.lineTo(px, py)
    if close:
        ctx.closePath()


def _text(ctx, text, at, align, baseline, dx=0, dy=0):
    x, y = _px(*at)
    ctx.textAlign = align
    ctx.textBaseline = baseline
    ctx.fillText(text, x + dx, y + dy)

"""The polymer-mix legend: a PCA biplot of the samples' polymer mixes over the stretched color
wheel that colors them (export_web_map.polymer_wheel), drawn on a canvas."""
import math

import js
from antioch.elements import Canvas

from . import config as c
from .labels import place_label

WIDTH, HEIGHT = 300, 290  # CSS pixels
CENTER = (WIDTH / 2, 134)
SCALE = 82                 # pixels per plot unit (the farthest sample is at 1); leaves room
                           # for the rim labels inside the canvas
RIM_GAP = 8                # anchor labels sit this far outside the wheel
ANCHOR_FONT = f"600 10.5px {c.FONT}"
POINT_FONT = f"600 10px {c.FONT}"
AXIS_FONT = f"10px {c.FONT}"


def wheel_key(spec):
    """A Canvas drawing the wheel's cells, the polymer lines and the numbered samples."""
    ratio = js.window.devicePixelRatio or 1
    canvas = Canvas(width=int(WIDTH * ratio), height=int(HEIGHT * ratio),
                    style={"width": f"{WIDTH}px", "height": f"{HEIGHT}px", "display": "block",
                           "margin": "4px 0 6px"})
    ctx = canvas.dom_element.getContext("2d")
    ctx.scale(ratio, ratio)

    for cell in spec["cells"]:
        *xy, color = cell
        _path(ctx, list(zip(xy[0::2], xy[1::2])))
        ctx.fillStyle = color
        ctx.strokeStyle = color  # hairline in the same color closes the seams between cells
        ctx.lineWidth = 0.6
        ctx.fill()
        ctx.stroke()

    # PC axes, faint; the share of variance they hold is the caption.
    ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6)"
    ctx.lineWidth = 0.8
    r = spec["radius"]
    for line in ([(-r, 0), (r, 0)], [(0, -r), (0, r)]):
        _path(ctx, line, close=False)
        ctx.stroke()
    ctx.fillStyle = c.INK_MUTED
    ctx.font = AXIS_FONT
    ctx.textAlign = "center"
    ctx.textBaseline = "bottom"
    ctx.fillText(f"{spec['axes'][0]} across · {spec['axes'][1]} up, of the variance",
                 WIDTH / 2, HEIGHT - 2)

    # Polymer lines from the center: the anchors (which set the hues) heavier and labelled
    # just outside the rim, in their direction; the rest faint and unlabelled.
    for line in spec["lines"]:
        _path(ctx, [(0, 0), (line["x"], line["y"])], close=False)
        ctx.strokeStyle = c.POPUP_INK if line["anchor"] else "rgba(11, 11, 11, 0.4)"
        ctx.lineWidth = 1.4 if line["anchor"] else 0.8
        ctx.stroke()
        if not line["anchor"]:
            continue
        length = math.hypot(line["x"], line["y"]) or 1
        ux, uy = line["x"] / length, line["y"] / length
        x, y = _px(ux * r, uy * r)
        ctx.font = ANCHOR_FONT
        ctx.fillStyle = c.INK
        ctx.textAlign = "left" if ux > 0.3 else "right" if ux < -0.3 else "center"
        ctx.textBaseline = "top" if uy < -0.3 else "bottom" if uy > 0.3 else "middle"
        ctx.fillText(line["label"], x + RIM_GAP * ux, y - RIM_GAP * uy)

    # Samples: a dot in the color its watershed gets, numbered.
    placed = []
    for point in spec["points"]:
        x, y = _px(point["x"], point["y"])
        ctx.beginPath()
        ctx.arc(x, y, 6, 0, 2 * math.pi)
        ctx.fillStyle = point["color"]
        ctx.fill()
        ctx.lineWidth = 1.5
        ctx.strokeStyle = c.OUTLINE
        ctx.stroke()
        ctx.beginPath()
        ctx.arc(x, y, 7, 0, 2 * math.pi)
        ctx.lineWidth = 0.75
        ctx.strokeStyle = c.POPUP_INK
        ctx.stroke()
        ctx.font = POINT_FONT
        ctx.fillStyle = c.POPUP_INK
        place_label(ctx, point["label"], x, y, placed)
    return canvas


def _px(x, y):
    return CENTER[0] + x * SCALE, CENTER[1] - y * SCALE


def _path(ctx, points, close=True):
    ctx.beginPath()
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(points):
        px, py = _px(x, y)
        if i == 0:
            ctx.moveTo(px, py)
        else:
            ctx.lineTo(px, py)
    if close:
        ctx.closePath()
